name: The Loom Braid
description: The Ninjacat Skies storyline, in order.

pages.title: This is the storyline
pages.text:
Nine Strands. Seat each token at a **Tension Post**. That is the campaign. Side chapters (sieve, storage, bees-as-a-board) are optional depth — they are not the story.

1. **Wake — Soil.** Claim a pad. Soil Knot → seat Soil.
2. **Recover — Stone.** Yarn, knots, meshes. Stone Knot → seat Stone.
3. **Root — Sprout.** Food and essence. Sprout Knot → seat Sprout.
4. **Edge — Claw.** Kit up and leave the pad on purpose. Claw Knot → seat Claw. The braid opens.

pages.title: Peers, then the close
pages.text:
5–7. **Pattern / Colony / Hum** — Clock, Swarm, Spark. Peers. Any **two** seated unlock Bind. You do not have to finish all three.
8. **Bind — Sigil.** Spin **Braid Cord** at the Post (a Strand Filament, two peers seated). Sigil Knot → seat Sigil.
9. **Reweave — Spindle.** Digital loom, Gate Drum, a March stone. All nine seated, stone on the Post → the Fragment. Seat the Fragment. The cut closes above your pad.

pages.title: Why this order
pages.text:
Soil before Stone because a pad has to stay warm before it can hold a mesh. Sprout before Claw because you leave on purpose, not because you are starving. Claw before the peers because Edge-walkers never asked anyone to be brave in the same place twice — pick a way.

Bind is three Strands agreeing in public. Reweave is nine. The old world broke when maintenance stopped. This order is maintenance, written down.

pages.title: Mending, not restoring
pages.text:
Reweave does not put the hanging continents back. It does not un-scatter the tribes. It teaches nine Strands to hold a pad, then a Dock, then a sky that is honest about being thread.

The Fray over the Dock is the public clock. It thins when a Clowder reweaves. It turns to lit thread when every Clowder has done the same. Look at it. If it is still dark, someone else still has work.

pages.title: Help the next Clowder
pages.text:
When your Fragment is seated, your Strand of the sky has closed. The next Clowder still has nine promises to keep. Share a mesh. Walk their pad. Sit at their drum.

The March kept the tablets and the Silent Drum. Read the halls. Strike four beats, a breath apart, when you are ready. Tell the camps we are sorry it took so long — then make sure it does not take that long for the next team.
